title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a typed and hand-corrected draft page of EGA IV, numbered IV-977-23, section (18.13) 'module de différentielles analytiques'. It has evidently ended up as scrap paper in the 'Cristaux' file: the neighbouring handwritten pages on divided powers π^{(n)} are unrelated to it.

Setting. For topological rings that are noetherian and semi-local with their preadic (Jacobson-adic) topologies, Grothendieck works with a module Ω̄^1_{B/A}. It is a quotient of the Kähler module Ω^1_{B/A} meant to capture 'analytic' differentials. When it is of finite type it is characterised as follows: Ω̄^1_{B/A} together with d̄_{B/A} represents L ↦ Dér_A(B,L) on the category of B-modules of finite type.

First paragraph (end of a proof). The page opens mid-word ('[co]ïncide'). Suppose Ω̄^1_{A/k} is of finite type. By (0,20.4.8), d̄_{A/k} factors as A → Ω^1_{A/k} → Ω̄^1_{A/k} through a map u_0. Every A-linear u: Ω^1_{A/k} → L with L of finite type then factors through u_0, so Ker(u) ⊇ Ker(u_0). The assertion being proved is therefore that this module coincides with the 18.13.1 definition: the quotient of Ω^1 by the intersection of the kernels of all maps to finite modules.

Remark. If Ω̄^1_{B/A} is of finite type, it represents L ↦ Dér_A(B,L) on finite B-modules. If Ω^1_{B/A} is itself of finite type, then Ω̄^1_{B/A} = Ω^1_{B/A}; by (0,20.4.7) this happens for instance when B is an A-algebra of finite type.

Proposition 18.13.5. Let A be a topological ring and B, C topological A-algebras that are noetherian semi-local rings with preadic topologies, with ρ: B → C a continuous A-homomorphism.
- (i) If Ω̄_{C/A} is finite, then Ω̄_{C/B} is finite.
- (ii) If Ω̄_{B/A} is finite and C is finite over B, then Ω̄_{C/A} is finite.
- (iii) Under the hypotheses of (ii), or under those of (i) plus Ω_{B/A} finite, there are C-maps ū and v̄ making diagram (18.13.5.1) commute. The diagram maps the first fundamental exact sequence Ω_{B/A}⊗C → Ω_{C/A} → Ω_{C/B} → 0 onto the bottom row Ω̄_{B/A}⊗C → Ω̄_{C/A} → Ω̄_{C/B} → 0. The page ends before the statement is complete; it presumably goes on to assert that the bottom row is exact.

In modern terms this is the first fundamental exact sequence for universally finite differential modules.
errors: The words 'déterminés de façon unique' are crossed out in (iii). Uniqueness of ū and v̄ follows from the universal property only when the bottom row's modules are known to be of finite type, so the deletion is a deliberate caution rather than an error.
In (i), Ω̄_{C/B} is a quotient of Ω̄_{C/A} because B-derivations are A-derivations. Finiteness is immediate, and the proof is not on this page.

ideas.what: Module Ω̄^1_{B/A} representing L ↦ Dér_A(B,L) on finite-type B-modules for noetherian semi-local topological algebras, described as Ω^1 modulo the intersection of kernels of maps to finite modules
ideas.modern_name: universally finite differential module (Kunz; Scheja–Storch), closely related to the completed differentials Ω̂
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Scheja and U. Storch (1970s) and E. Kunz, 'Kähler Differentials' (1986); completed differentials are in EGA 0_IV §20.7
ideas.where_published: EGA 0_IV §20.7 treats completed differentials Ω̂. A section numbered 18.13 on 'différentielles analytiques' does not, to my knowledge, appear in the published EGA IV §18, so this draft may be a suppressed section.

ideas.what: First fundamental exact sequence for Ω̄ under finiteness hypotheses (B → C finite, or Ω_{B/A} finite)
ideas.modern_name: fundamental exact sequence for universally finite differential modules
ideas.where_published: Analogues for Ω̂ are in EGA 0_IV 20.7.

ideas.what: Ω̄ = Ω when Ω is of finite type, e.g. B of finite type over A (0,20.4.7)
ideas.modern_name: trivial case of the universally finite module
ideas.where_published: EGA 0_IV 20.4.7 (finiteness of Ω for finite-type algebras)

missed.claim: An EGA IV draft section (18.13) develops 'analytic differentials' Ω̄ for noetherian semi-local topological algebras. It defines them by representability on finite modules, i.e. it is essentially the universally finite differential module, together with its fundamental exact sequence and finiteness permanence. This seems to predate the Scheja–Storch/Kunz theory, and the section apparently did not survive into the published EGA IV.
missed.quote: si $\bar\Omega^1_{B/A}$ est un B-module de type fini , il représente le foncteur covariant $L \rightsquigarrow \mathrm{Dér}_A(B,L)$ dans la catégorie des B-modules de type fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point: Grothendieck's EGA drafts contained the universally finite differential module concept. The results themselves are standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine EGA-style draft, but it may be an unpublished section 18.13 anticipating universally finite differential modules. Its interest is historical only.
transcription_corrections: The first word is '[co]ïncide', the start of 'coïncide' with the prefix on the previous sheet.
The header reads '- IV-977 -23-', with 977 handwritten.
The marginal handwritten note next to (iii) is illegible and probably reads something like 'style ... ' with a correction mark; the crossed-out word below it is 'façon'.
The bottom-right handwritten '45' is the archive page number.
